name: Weights pass through the crossing
aliases: naturality of the fermionic swap for weights
summary: A binary white vertex (weight r) moves through a fermionic crossing from one wire to the other.
description:
The *crossing* (fermionic swap) of the ZW-calculus is the map $|00\rangle\langle 00| + |01\rangle\langle 10| + |10\rangle\langle 01| - |11\rangle\langle 11|$: a swap that picks up a sign $-1$ when two $|1\rangle$'s (two fermions) are exchanged. It equals a SWAP followed by a CZ. It behaves like a symmetric braiding, except that it is only natural for *even* maps (those whose terms all have an even number of 1s); maps of odd parity, such as the black vertices, pick up signs. 

The binary white vertex $\mathrm{diag}(1, r)$ (a weight $r$ on an edge, drawn as a Z-box) is even, so the crossing is natural with respect to it: a weight on a wire after the crossing equals the same weight on that wire before the crossing. In the planar W-calculus of Carette et al. the fermionic swap is not a generator but syntactic sugar for a gadget of black and white vertices; this axiom is one of the rules governing it.
unchecked_reason: uses the fermionic crossing of the ZW-calculus, which is not a PyZX generator
